_about: Defect classes for this repository, read by projectos.infrastructure.defect_sweep. Declarations (name, source, instances, enforcement_test) are founder-owned and hand-written; the sweep only ever adds an observed 'last_sweep' block. A class is closed when its enforcement test makes a NEW instance fail the build.

DC-7.name: Unauthenticated instruction channel
DC-7.description: Every seat takes instructions from files in one Drive folder with no signature and no way to tell an issuer's assignment from a file that simply appeared. Seats run on the founder's own identity, so a seat acting on a bad instruction acts as him. The protection is written here as ABSENT-until-adopted, not as present because a module exists.
DC-7.source: Assignment INBOX-TRUST-BOUNDARY, 2026-08-15; DC-6 discipline: a protection that does not exist is written as absent
DC-7.what_exists: The mechanism: projectos.infrastructure.inbox_auth (HMAC-SHA256 stamp, key out-of-band, fail-closed verify, refusal reported). Built and tested 2026-08-17.
DC-7.what_is_absent: Adoption. No issuer signs yet and no seat verifies-before-acting yet, so the channel itself is still open. The mechanism cannot be armed unilaterally by one seat: an enforcing seat would refuse every currently-legitimate unsigned assignment.
DC-7.closes_when: Issuers sign every assignment (Chat holds the key in its instructions), every seat verifies before acting, and the wake scheduler gates on verification. MUST close before the wake is armed — after arming, no human reads a file before a seat acts on it.
DC-7.tier_note: Authentication does not raise a file's tier. An authenticated ESCALATE ask is still refused; being genuine is not being authorised. Pinned by test.

DC-1.name: A value believed rather than observed
DC-1.description: A claim accepted because something reported it, rather than because it was read from the thing itself. The general form of every trust-the-report defect: an exit code trusted instead of a parsed summary, a seat tag trusted instead of a repo root, a clock trusted instead of an anchored instant.
DC-1.source: TradeOS observed-fact rule (DC-1); extended to fleet time by assignment FLEET-CLOCK, 2026-08-14

instances.what: `TZ='Asia/Kolkata' date` returned GMT with no tzdata present and no error, putting reported times 5.5 hours out.
instances.why_it_is_this_class: A timezone was requested and the answer believed; the offset was never checked against anything.
instances.now_caught_by: now_ist() converts by a fixed +05:30 offset and never depends on a named-zone lookup; tzdata is consulted only as a cross-check that raises on disagreement.

instances.who: Chat — and Chat only. No seat instance has been measured: seat-written stamps measure at 4s against Drive server time, so the seats' clocks are sound and this family is not fleet-wide.
instances.what: Chat stamped filenames and prose dates from an assumed time rather than a read one, on MORE THAN THREE occasions. Measured against Drive's server-side timestamps on 2026-08-15: 162 minutes, 21.7, 17.9, 5.2.
instances.magnitude_status: MEASURED against Drive server time (supersedes the 2026-08-14 UNVERIFIED statement)
instances.measured_by: Chat, running the Chat-owned half of the split check against Drive createdTime/modifiedTime — its first real run, and it caught its own author.
instances.fifth_instance: 2026-08-15: a competitor note stamped 2026-08-14 while Drive read 2026-08-15. Recorded because the count is 'more than three', not exactly three.
instances.rule_adopted_by_chat: Read Drive before writing any date, in a filename or in prose.
instances.why_it_is_this_class: The time was supplied from belief rather than read. It sorts, so it corrupts 'oldest file first' ordering silently.

amendment_history.said: At least three occasions, MAGNITUDE UNVERIFIED — a 64-minute figure had been attributed to Chat's clock error, but it was measured against the local mirror's mtime, which for a synced file is the sync write, so clock error and sync latency were not separable from a seat.
amendment_history.why: The anchor problem it named was real and the fix was to split the check, not to widen a tolerance. Once the Chat-owned half ran against the correct anchor, the magnitude stopped being unknowable. Superseded, not deleted: the earlier statement was honest about what could be seen at the time.

instances.now_caught_by: stamp_for_filename() is the single way to produce a stamp and raises rather than returning a plausible time when the clock cannot be established. For synced files the magnitude is visible only against Drive's server-side timestamp — the Chat-owned half of the split check, now demonstrated live.

DC-1.tolerance: DECLARED by the founder on 2026-08-14 at 120s on the resolution argument — see docs/parameter_registry.json (FLEET-CLOCK-SKEW-TOLERANCE). Code still has no default: it resolves the value and fails closed when absent.
DC-1.check_ownership: Split by anchor, ruled 2026-08-14. Locally-written files: PROJECTOS, via check_local_file against local mtime (the authoring moment here). Synced files: CHAT, against Drive's server-side createdTime/modifiedTime — this seat cannot see that fact and refuses the check rather than measuring sync latency and calling it clock error.
DC-1.split_validated: 2026-08-15. Both halves have now run against real files. Chat's half produced measured magnitudes (worst 162 minutes) and caught the participant who owns it; the local half measured seat-written stamps at 4s. The seat that could not see the fact would have reported sync latency as clock error, and the seat that could see it found a real 162-minute error — which is the whole argument for assigning a check to whoever can see the fact.
